summary.text: Mike Bost is the Republican U.S. Representative for Illinois's 12th District, in office since January 2015, and won re-election on November 3, 2026, according to unofficial results.

A Murphysboro native and Marine Corps veteran, he worked in his family's trucking business and as a firefighter before serving 20 years in the Illinois House. He chairs the House Veterans' Affairs Committee.

paragraphs.text: Bost was born and raised in Murphysboro, Illinois, and graduated from Murphysboro High School in 1979.
He served in the U.S. Marine Corps from 1979 to 1982 as an electronic specialist and radar repairman, receiving an honorable discharge as a Corporal E-4.
He then worked 13 years at Bost Trucking Service, first as a driver and then as a truck manager, until his election to the Illinois legislature.
Bost served on the Jackson County Board (1984-1988) and as Treasurer of Murphysboro Township (1989-1992), then became a Murphysboro trustee in 1993.

That year he also became a certified firefighter through the University of Illinois Firefighter Academy, and he served with the Murphysboro Fire Department, including during six of his terms as a state representative.
He served in the Illinois House of Representatives, District 115, from 1995 to 2014, rising to House Republican Caucus Chair.
Bost was sworn into the U.S. House on January 6, 2015. In the 119th Congress he serves on the Veterans' Affairs (Chairman), Transportation and Infrastructure, and Agriculture committees.
According to his House biography, he and his wife, Tracy, own the White House Salon in Murphysboro; they have three children and eleven grandchildren.
He won re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election with 69.7% of the vote to Julie Fortier's 30.3%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
